LESSON: WRITING 13.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it difficult to spell some words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words
2. form new words using prefixes and suffixes
3. spell words correctly for writing fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 13.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 13.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Form new words using prefixes and suffixes

What this means
In this part you learn to form new words using prefixes and suffixes. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: form new words using prefixes and suffixes.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can form new words using prefixes and suffixes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Spell words correctly for writing fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to spell words correctly for writing fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell words correctly for writing fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell words correctly for writing fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing to a partner. (skill: form new words using prefixes and suffixes)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: spell words correctly for writing fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words.
3. Practise this skill: form new words using prefixes and suffixes.
4. Practise this skill: spell words correctly for writing fluency.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it difficult to spell some words?
2. How can we become better at spelling?
3. what went well and why?
4. what did not go well and why?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise affixes used to change the form and meaning of words.
5. Be able to: form new words using prefixes and suffixes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
